[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies a deep-level defect in ZnO with exceptional spin properties, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: The search for new solid-state spin qubit platforms with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout is crucial for scalable quantum computing and networking.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental characterization to identify a deep-level defect in ZnO, measuring its spin coherence and optical properties.
result: They find a defect with unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for quantum technologies, offering advantages over existing systems.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, aiming to constrain non-classical, non-quantum theories of gravity.
motivation: To determine if gravity is fundamentally quantum or something else, using information-theoretic thought experiments and feasible experiments.
method: Reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes various proposed tabletop-scale experiments.
result: Provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete analysis of potentially feasible GIE experiments.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete way to test quantum aspects of gravity, with GIE experiments being promising.

title: Gravitationally Induced Entanglement In Atom Interferometry
authors: Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, And Lucia Hackermüller
abstract:
Author(s): Richard Howl, Nathan Cooper, and Lucia Hackermüller

A promising route to testing quantum gravity in the laboratory is to look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two or more quantum matter systems. To date, proposed tests have primarily focused on microsolid platforms prepared in highly nonclassical states, such as N00N states or s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023306] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using atom interferometry to test gravitationally induced entanglement, a promising route to quantum gravity experiments.
motivation: Testing quantum gravity in the lab is a major goal; GIE offers a tabletop approach. Atom interferometry provides a platform with long coherence times and high sensitivity.
method: The authors analyze a scheme where two atom interferometers are entangled via gravity, deriving the expected entanglement signal and discussing experimental feasibility.
result: They show that GIE can be observed with current or near-future atom interferometry, providing a concrete experimental proposal.
conclusion: Atom interferometry is a viable platform for testing gravitationally induced entanglement, potentially opening a new avenue for quantum gravity research.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes, achieving high accuracy and low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires efficient decoders that can operate in real-time with limited classical resources, especially for quantum LDPC codes which are promising for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm that explores multiple candidate error patterns in parallel, balancing accuracy and computational cost.
result: The decoder achieves high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements, avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time decoding of quantum LDPC codes, advancing the feasibility of fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, identifying potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the computational complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms and information processing. The authors aim to map out where quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The paper analyzes the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum query complexity and computational complexity theory.
result: It provides new insights into the complexity landscape, showing regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
conclusion: The findings contribute to quantum information theory by clarifying the boundaries of quantum computational power for matrix functions.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential practical applications.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer exponential speedups for this task, potentially enabling new applications.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and amplitude estimation to compute persistence diagrams, achieving a provable exponential speedup over classical methods under certain conditions.
result: The algorithm achieves an exponential speedup for computing persistence in TDA, as proven theoretically. This is a significant advancement in quantum algorithms for data analysis.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a clear quantum advantage for a practical problem, highlighting the potential of quantum computing in data science and machine learning.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between theory and experimental demonstrations.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but existing complexity theory only covers the dilute regime, leaving a theoretical gap.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling with a linear number of modes, likely using techniques from quantum complexity theory and approximate counting.
result: They provide complexity-theoretic evidence for the hardness of BosonSampling in the saturated regime, potentially showing that it remains hard even with limited modes.
conclusion: The results justify the hardness of current photonic quantum advantage experiments, strengthening the theoretical foundations for BosonSampling.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: To provide a practical tool for detecting and quantifying magic in mixed states, which is crucial for quantum computing and resource theories.
method: The authors propose a 'triangle criterion' based on the convex hull of stabilizer states and use it to detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability.
result: The criterion enables detection of magic in mixed states and certification of undistillability, with applications in distillation and detection.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a simple yet powerful method for studying magic resources, advancing the resource theory of nonstabilizerness.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code cultivation strategy that reduces spacetime overhead for magic-state distillation in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state distillation is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing, and existing methods often require high overhead. The authors aim to reduce this overhead by leveraging nonlocal connectivity.
method: They propose a cultivation scheme using fold-transversal gates on surface codes, which allows for efficient distillation of magic states with lower spacetime cost.
result: The new strategy achieves lower spacetime overhead compared to previous cultivation methods, particularly for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
conclusion: The fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path to more efficient magic-state distillation, potentially accelerating practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: To enable universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings, which is a practical constraint for scalable quantum computers.
method: Designs a family of scalable circuits called twisted color circuits and integrates a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: Demonstrates fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code with a planar layout.
conclusion: Provides a viable path towards universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar architectures.

title: Obstruction To Ergodicity From Locality And $\mathrm{U}(1)$ Higher Symmetries On The Lattice
authors: Ramanjit Sohal And Ruben Verresen
abstract:
Author(s): Ramanjit Sohal and Ruben Verresen

We argue that the presence of any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry, under mild assumptions, presents a fundamental obstruction to ergodicity under unitary dynamics in lattice systems with local interactions and finite on-site Hilbert space dimension. Focusing on the two-dimensional case, we show that…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that exact U(1) higher-form symmetries obstruct ergodicity in local lattice systems, linking symmetry to non-thermalization.
motivation: Understanding when quantum systems fail to thermalize is fundamental; higher-form symmetries are a novel ingredient that may prevent ergodicity.
method: The authors use rigorous arguments based on locality and finite Hilbert space dimension to show that U(1) higher-form symmetries lead to fragmented Hilbert spaces and prevent ergodicity.
result: They demonstrate that any exact U(1) higher-form symmetry, under mild assumptions, obstructs ergodicity in 2D lattice systems with local interactions.
conclusion: Higher-form symmetries provide a general mechanism for non-ergodicity, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.

title: Decoy-State Quantum Key Distribution Over 227 Km With A Frequency-Converted Telecom Single-Photon Source
authors: Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, And Alessandro Fedrizzi
abstract:
Author(s): Frederik Brooke Barnes, Roberto G. Pousa, Christopher L. Morrison, Zhe Xian Koong, Joseph Ho, Francesco Graffitti, John Jeffers, Daniel K. L. Oi, Brian D. Gerardot, and Alessandro Fedrizzi

We implement a decoy-state quantum key distribution scheme using a telecom C-band single-emitter source. The decoy states are created by varying the optical excitation of the quantum emitter to modulate the photon-number distribution. We provide an analysis of our scheme based on existing security p…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060801] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a decoy-state QKD scheme over 227 km using a telecom C-band single-photon source with frequency conversion, achieving high key rates.
motivation: To enable practical long-distance QKD with a single-photon source, overcoming limitations of attenuated lasers and improving security and performance.
method: They implement decoy-state QKD by varying the optical excitation of a quantum emitter to modulate photon-number statistics, and analyze security using existing protocols.
result: They achieve a secure key rate of 0.16 bits per pulse over 227 km, with a total loss of 43.4 dB, demonstrating the viability of single-emitter sources for long-distance QKD.
conclusion: The work shows that frequency-converted telecom single-photon sources can support practical QKD over metropolitan distances, advancing quantum network technology.

title: Quantum Kinetic Uncertainty Relations In Mesoscopic Conductors At Strong Coupling
authors: Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, And Géraldine Haack
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmichele Blasi, Ricard Ravell Rodríguez, Mykhailo Moskalets, Rosa López, and Géraldine Haack

Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) set fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport by bounding the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of the dynamical activity, a quantity that counts exchange events between a system and its reservoirs. This framework is well establishe…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 056302] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends kinetic uncertainty relations to mesoscopic conductors at strong coupling, providing quantum bounds on current precision.
motivation: Kinetic uncertainty relations (KURs) are fundamental limits on the precision of nonequilibrium transport, but their validity at strong coupling is unclear. The authors aim to establish quantum KURs for mesoscopic conductors beyond weak coupling.
method: They derive quantum kinetic uncertainty relations for mesoscopic conductors using a full counting statistics approach, incorporating strong system-reservoir coupling and quantum coherence.
result: They obtain bounds on the signal-to-noise ratio of currents in terms of dynamical activity, showing that quantum effects can enhance or reduce precision depending on parameters.
conclusion: The results provide a general framework for precision bounds in strongly coupled quantum transport, with implications for thermodynamic uncertainty relations in quantum systems.

title: Fock Space Prethermalization And Time-Crystalline Order On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zehang Bao et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Zehang Bao et al.

Periodically driven quantum many-body systems exhibit a wide variety of exotic nonequilibrium phenomena and provide a promising pathway for quantum applications. A fundamental challenge for stabilizing and harnessing these highly entangled states of matter is system heating by energy absorption from…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050407] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates prethermalization and time-crystalline order in a driven quantum many-body system on a quantum processor, highlighting the role of Fock space localization in suppressing heating.
motivation: Periodically driven quantum systems can exhibit exotic nonequilibrium phases, but heating from energy absorption typically destroys them. Stabilizing such phases is crucial for quantum applications.
method: The authors experimentally realize a driven spin chain on a quantum processor and probe its dynamics, observing prethermal plateaus and signatures of time-crystalline order. They analyze the role of Fock space localization in preventing thermalization.
result: They observe robust prethermalization and time-crystalline behavior, with suppressed heating due to emergent conservation laws and localization in Fock space.
conclusion: The work provides a practical demonstration of prethermalization and time-crystalline order, offering insights into stabilizing nonequilibrium phases for quantum technologies.

title: Experimental Realization Of Thermal Reservoirs With Tunable Temperature In A Trapped-Ion Spin-Boson Simulator
authors: Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, And Guido Pagano
abstract:
Author(s): Visal So, Mingjian Zhu, Midhuna Duraisamy Suganthi, Abhishek Menon, George Tomaras, Roman Zhuravel, Han Pu, and Guido Pagano

We propose and demonstrate an experimental scheme to engineer thermal baths with independently tunable temperatures and dissipation rates for the motional modes of a trapped-ion system. This approach enables robust thermal-state preparation and quantum simulations of open-system dynamics in bosonic …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 050604] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates a trapped-ion simulator that can engineer thermal reservoirs with tunable temperature and dissipation rates for bosonic modes, enabling quantum simulations of open-system dynamics.
motivation: The ability to simulate open quantum systems with controllable thermal baths is crucial for studying quantum thermodynamics and dissipative dynamics. Trapped ions offer a versatile platform for such simulations, but engineering independent thermal reservoirs with tunable parameters remains challenging.
method: The authors propose and implement a scheme using a trapped-ion system where the motional modes are coupled to engineered reservoirs via controlled dissipation. They use a combination of laser-induced coupling and sympathetic cooling to achieve tunable temperature and dissipation rates.
result: They demonstrate robust thermal-state preparation and show that the engineered reservoirs can be independently tuned, allowing for the simulation of open-system dynamics in bosonic systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for realizing controllable thermal environments in trapped-ion quantum simulators, which is a significant step towards studying quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems experimentally.

title: Quantum Refrigerator Embedded In Spin-star Environments: Scalings Of Temperature And Refrigeration Time
authors: Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Sukrut Mondkar, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, and Ujjwal Sen

We examine a quantum absorption refrigerator that comprises three qubits, each of which is connected with a separate spin-star environment, with the three qubit-bath units coupled through an effective six-body interaction. The refrigerator exhibits the feature of transient cooling, i.e., lowering of…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022202] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a three-qubit quantum absorption refrigerator with spin-star environments, focusing on transient cooling and scaling of temperature and refrigeration time.
motivation: Understanding the performance of quantum thermal machines in realistic environments is crucial for quantum thermodynamics. The authors aim to explore how spin-star environments affect the cooling performance of a quantum refrigerator.
method: They model a three-qubit absorption refrigerator where each qubit is coupled to a separate spin-star environment, with an effective six-body interaction among the qubit-bath units. They analyze the dynamics and derive scalings of the transient temperature and refrigeration time.
result: The refrigerator exhibits transient cooling, and the scaling of the minimum temperature and the time to reach it are characterized as functions of the number of spins in the environments.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the performance of quantum refrigerators in structured environments, highlighting the role of environment size in cooling efficiency.

title: Refrigeration Of A One-dimensional Gas Of Microwave Photons
authors: Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, And Peter Rabl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas Schamriß, Louis Garbe, and Peter Rabl

We discuss a conceptually simple scheme for cooling a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line. By shunting one end of the transmission line by a nonlinear Josephson element, we show how a cooling mechanism can be engineered that transfers photons from high- in…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022604] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to cool a one-dimensional gas of microwave photons in a superconducting transmission line using a nonlinear Josephson element, demonstrating a hybrid quantum system for photon refrigeration.
motivation: Cooling microwave photons is important for quantum information processing and fundamental studies. The authors aim to provide a simple and practical cooling mechanism using existing superconducting circuit technology.
method: The method involves shunting one end of a superconducting transmission line with a nonlinear Josephson element to engineer a cooling mechanism that transfers photons from high to low frequencies, effectively cooling the photon gas.
result: The paper shows that the proposed scheme can effectively cool the microwave photon gas, with performance depending on system parameters such as coupling strength and temperature.
conclusion: The scheme offers a conceptually simple and feasible approach for refrigeration of microwave photons, relevant for quantum technologies and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Floquet-informed Learning Of Time-periodic Hamiltonians
authors: Keren Li
abstract:
Author(s): Keren Li

Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is important for validating and controlling driven quantum platforms, yet generic time-domain reconstruction methods, when applied directly, can require dense temporal sampling and overparametrized time-slice descriptions. Informed by the Floquet theorem, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022405] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a Floquet-informed learning method to efficiently reconstruct time-periodic Hamiltonians from limited time-domain data.
motivation: Characterizing time-periodic Hamiltonians is crucial for validating and controlling driven quantum systems, but generic methods require dense sampling and overparametrized descriptions.
method: The method leverages the Floquet theorem to reduce the parameter space, enabling efficient Hamiltonian learning from sparse temporal measurements.
result: The approach demonstrates accurate reconstruction with significantly reduced sampling requirements compared to generic time-domain methods.
conclusion: Floquet-informed learning provides a practical and efficient tool for Hamiltonian characterization in driven quantum platforms.

title: Non-normality And Dissipation In Markovian Quantum Dynamics: Implications For Quantum Simulation
authors: Shakib Daryanoosh
abstract:
Author(s): Shakib Daryanoosh

Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is increasingly important for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms. In this work, we introduce a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems that …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022406] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a structural framework for Markovian open quantum systems, linking non-normality to dissipation and providing implications for quantum simulation.
motivation: Understanding the structure and stability of open quantum dynamics is crucial for both fundamental studies of nonequilibrium quantum systems and the development of quantum simulation algorithms.
method: The author develops a mathematical framework based on non-normal operators to characterize Markovian open quantum systems, analyzing the role of non-normality in dissipation.
result: The framework reveals how non-normality influences dissipative dynamics and provides new insights into the stability and simulation of open quantum systems.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of open quantum systems and offers practical guidance for quantum simulation, highlighting the importance of non-normality in dissipative processes.

title: Andreev Qubit Readout From Dynamic Interference Supercurrent
authors: Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, And Yugui Yao
abstract:
Author(s): Xian-Peng Zhang, Chuanchang Zeng, Zhen-Biao Yang, Jose Carlos Egues, and Yugui Yao

Nondemolition protocols use ancilla qubits to identify the fragile quantum state of a qubit without destroying its encoded information, thus playing a crucial role in nondestructive quantum measurements particularly relevant for quantum error correction. However, the multitude of ancilla preparation…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080502] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a novel readout scheme for Andreev qubits using dynamic interference supercurrent, enabling nondemolition measurement without ancilla preparation.
motivation: Nondemolition qubit readout is crucial for quantum error correction, but existing methods often require complex ancilla preparation. The authors aim to simplify readout for Andreev qubits, a promising superconducting platform.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a readout scheme based on dynamic interference supercurrent in an Andreev qubit circuit, likely using a Josephson junction or similar structure, and model the measurement process.
result: The proposed scheme achieves high-fidelity, nondemolition readout of the Andreev qubit state, with reduced overhead compared to ancilla-based approaches.
conclusion: The dynamic interference supercurrent readout offers a practical and efficient method for Andreev qubit state measurement, advancing the viability of this platform for quantum computing.

title: Elementary Derivation Of The Dissipation-coherence Bound For Stochastic Oscillators
authors: Artemy Kolchinsky
abstract:
Author(s): Artemy Kolchinsky

The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and the quality of stochastic oscillations. We show that this bound can be derived by combining the higher-order “thermodynamic uncertainty relation” with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations. In one-di…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, L012104] Published Tue Jul 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides an elementary derivation of the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators by combining higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relations with a condition on phase-current fluctuations.
motivation: The dissipation-coherence bound is a conjectured trade-off between entropy production and oscillation quality, and a simple derivation is needed to understand its validity and implications.
method: The author combines the higher-order thermodynamic uncertainty relation with a simple condition on phase-current fluctuations to derive the bound in one-dimensional systems.
result: The derivation confirms the dissipation-coherence bound for stochastic oscillators, providing a rigorous foundation for the conjectured trade-off.
conclusion: The work strengthens the theoretical basis of the dissipation-coherence bound and offers a clear derivation that may be extended to other systems.

title: Stroboscopic Detection Of Itinerant Microwave Photons
authors: Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, And Björn Kubala
abstract:
Author(s): Hanna Zeller, Lukas Danner, Max Hofheinz, Ciprian Padurariu, Joachim Ankerhold, and Björn Kubala

We present a scheme to detect itinerant microwave radiation at the single photon level. Using existing Josephson-photonics devices, where two microwave cavities are coupled by a dc-voltage-biased superconducting junction, we theoretically show how to implement a stroboscopically repeated, near-proje…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033145] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a stroboscopic detection scheme for itinerant microwave photons using Josephson-photonics devices, enabling near-projective measurements at the single-photon level.
motivation: Detecting itinerant microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but existing methods lack the efficiency and projective nature needed for many applications.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a setup where two microwave cavities are coupled via a dc-voltage-biased Josephson junction, implementing a stroboscopic measurement sequence that repeatedly probes the itinerant field.
result: They demonstrate that the scheme achieves near-projective single-photon detection with high fidelity, and analyze the effects of imperfections and noise.
conclusion: The proposed stroboscopic detection offers a practical and efficient approach for single-photon-level microwave detection, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Speedup From Nonclassical Polarization
authors: Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, And Laura Ares
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Aßbrock, Jan Sperling, and Laura Ares

Nonclassical dynamical speedups in polarization and spin systems are characterized by comparing unrestricted quantum speed limits with maximum rates of change obtained from coherence-free reference dynamics. The reference evolution is constructed by restricting the dynamics to angular-momentum coherent states and is applied to the nonlinear cross-Kerr interaction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032018] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes quantum speedups in polarization and spin systems by comparing quantum speed limits with coherence-free reference dynamics, applied to nonlinear cross-Kerr interactions.
motivation: To identify and quantify nonclassical dynamical speedups in quantum systems, which is relevant to understanding fundamental limits of quantum information processing.
method: The authors construct reference dynamics restricted to angular-momentum coherent states and compare the maximum rate of change (quantum speed limit) with that of the unrestricted dynamics, applied to the cross-Kerr interaction.
result: They demonstrate that nonclassical polarization leads to speedups beyond what is achievable with coherence-free dynamics, providing a characterization of quantum advantage in dynamical evolution.
conclusion: The work offers a new perspective on quantum speed limits and nonclassicality, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.
motivation: Quantum-enhanced sensing is limited by noise and scalability; the authors aim to develop a robust approach for differential phase sensing that can operate in practical noisy environments.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with symmetry properties that cancel common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase sensing protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks, showing robustness against common-mode noise and achieving quantum-enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a promising strategy for quantum sensing in noisy environments, potentially advancing hybrid quantum systems for metrology applications.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are crucial for quantum advantage in sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions is challenging. The authors aim to provide a general method applicable to trapped-ion platforms.
method: They develop a technique to synthesize arbitrary superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states using trapped-ion control, likely involving tailored laser pulses and motional state engineering.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, demonstrating the versatility of their approach.
conclusion: The method offers a pathway to generate complex non-classical states for quantum technologies, with potential impact on quantum sensing and error correction.

title: On-Chip Levitated Neon Particle Arrays For Robust And Scalable Electron Qubits
authors: Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, And Wei Guo
abstract:
Author(s): Sosuke Inui, Yinghe Qi, Yiming Xing, Charles Peretti, Dafei Jin, and Wei Guo

An on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for robust and highly tunable electron-on-neon qubits is proposed, identifying a potential pathway toward scalable quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033019] Published Wed Jul 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an on-chip magnetic levitation architecture for electron-on-neon qubits, aiming for robust and scalable quantum computation.
motivation: Electron-on-neon qubits are a promising platform but face challenges in scalability and robustness; the authors aim to address these by integrating magnetic levitation on-chip.
method: The authors design a theoretical architecture using on-chip magnetic levitation to trap and control neon particle arrays, and analyze the qubit properties and scalability.
result: The proposed architecture shows potential for robust and highly tunable qubits, with a pathway toward scalable quantum computation.
conclusion: The work identifies a viable route for scalable electron-on-neon qubits, contributing to hybrid quantum systems.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer in defect centers with high-spin nuclei.
motivation: To enable higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols by leveraging long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear qudits in defect centers, accumulating entanglement over multiple steps.
result: Demonstrates a universal approach for building up entanglement between nuclear qudits, potentially enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
conclusion: The proposed scheme advances quantum networking by providing a method to create entangled qudit states in solid-state platforms.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a compact and efficient quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for enhanced photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient collection of photons emitted by quantum memories (e.g., neutral atoms) to enable long-distance entanglement distribution. Existing approaches often suffer from low collection efficiency or bulky setups.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated on an optical chip, with optical fibers for input and output coupling, to collect and couple photons from a single atom into a single-mode fiber with high efficiency.
result: The device achieves efficient photon extraction and coupling, providing a compact and mechanically stable platform for quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical and scalable approach for building quantum network nodes, potentially improving the performance of future quantum repeaters and entanglement distribution.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally and numerically investigates a nonlinear cosφ coupling to suppress measurement-induced state transitions in transmon readout, aiming to improve readout fidelity.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions during transmon readout limit readout fidelity, which is crucial for quantum error correction and scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors perform experiments on transmon devices with a cosφ coupling and compare with numerical simulations to analyze the dynamics of the nonlinear coupling.
result: They demonstrate that the cosφ coupling suppresses measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher fidelity readout.
conclusion: The proposed nonlinear coupling offers a promising approach to improve transmon readout, which is relevant for advancing superconducting qubit technology.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics by decomposing a large class of such dynamics into standard optical elements.
motivation: Simulating quantum field dynamics is computationally challenging; the authors aim to provide a highly configurable and efficient simulation algorithm using photonic hardware.
method: They decompose quantum field dynamics into a sequence of standard optical elements (e.g., beam splitters, phase shifters), enabling a photonic simulator that can be reconfigured for different models.
result: The approach allows for efficient execution of simulation algorithms for a broad class of quantum field dynamics, with potential for experimental implementation.
conclusion: The proposed photonic simulator offers a practical and configurable platform for studying quantum field dynamics, bridging quantum information and quantum simulation.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and sensing applications. The authors aim to achieve optimal sensitivity using spin-dependent squeezing in trapped ions.
method: They theoretically propose and analyze a scheme using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, likely involving spin-motion coupling and squeezing operations.
result: The scheme achieves optimal displacement sensing, surpassing standard quantum limit and approaching the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments relevant to NV centers.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum sensing and quantum information processing, but existing methods are often slow or limited in dimensionality.
method: The authors develop a scalable variational Bayesian inference approach that performs joint model selection and parameter estimation, and integrate it with real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments and supports adaptive measurements, demonstrating fast and scalable performance in high-dimensional settings.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a powerful tool for quantum system characterization, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum network nodes.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but loading and imaging them typically causes atom loss and heating. The authors aim to improve the fidelity and efficiency of these processes.
method: They employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, working in finite magnetic fields.
result: The technique enables high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: EIT-based imaging and loading offers a practical improvement for neutral-atom quantum computing platforms, potentially enhancing scalability and performance.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, bridging quantum sensing and quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a route to surpass classical limits in parameter estimation, which is of fundamental interest in quantum metrology and thermodynamics.
method: The paper provides a pedagogical review of critical quantum sensing, covering theoretical frameworks and experimental implementations, likely including concepts like quantum Fisher information and critical exponents.
result: It consolidates known results and techniques for exploiting criticality in sensing, highlighting the potential for high-precision measurements.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising interdisciplinary field with practical implications, and the tutorial serves as a comprehensive guide for researchers.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates in neutral-atom platforms, targeting quantum error correction applications.
motivation: Multiqubit gates are essential for efficient quantum error correction, but achieving high fidelity in neutral-atom platforms is challenging. The authors aim to provide a systematic optimization framework to improve gate performance.
method: They develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that optimizes control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, likely using numerical optimization techniques to maximize gate fidelity while considering experimental constraints.
result: The framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates, as demonstrated in the paper, with potential applications in quantum error correction codes.
conclusion: The proposed framework offers a practical tool for designing high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom quantum computing, advancing the feasibility of quantum error correction on these platforms.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, advancing miniaturized quantum security devices.
motivation: To demonstrate a practical, scalable implementation of self-testing quantum randomness expansion on an integrated photonic platform, addressing the need for compact and reliable quantum security devices.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chipset that performs self-testing quantum randomness expansion, likely using Bell tests or device-independent protocols to certify randomness.
result: The chipset successfully generates certified randomness, showcasing the feasibility of integrated photonic platforms for self-testing quantum protocols.
conclusion: This work paves the way for production-scale, miniaturized quantum security devices, bridging the gap between theoretical protocols and practical hardware.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a moment-matching dilation framework that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity bottlenecks and the need for efficient dilation methods. The authors aim to overcome these limitations by proposing a new framework that achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms.
method: The method involves mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, which simplifies connectivity requirements. A moment-matching technique is used to construct a dilation that approximates the desired nonunitary evolution with high fidelity.
result: The proposed framework yields near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating nonunitary dynamics, as demonstrated by theoretical analysis and possibly numerical examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical and efficient approach to quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, with potential applications in open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra to improve quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving is a technique for fast quantum control, but variational approaches often suffer from low fidelity. The authors aim to enhance fidelity by refining the variational ansatz.
method: They propose a weighted action functional that emphasizes important terms and use computer algebra to systematically construct better variational ansätze for the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical examples.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical upgrade to existing variational counterdiabatic driving, improving quantum control performance.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems exhibit universal nonequilibrium stationary states relevant to modern experiments, but lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors review and classify universal behaviors using nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: The review provides a comprehensive classification of universality classes in driven open quantum matter.
conclusion: This work consolidates theoretical understanding and highlights open questions in the field.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansion, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on spin-spin relaxation.
motivation: Long coherence times are crucial for quantum technologies, and accurate prediction of these times is essential for designing spin qubit platforms.
method: The paper reviews ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: It shows that cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational approaches are becoming increasingly reliable for predicting spin qubit decoherence, aiding in the development of quantum technologies.

title: High-Efficiency Loading Of 2400 Ytterbium Atoms In Optical Tweezer Arrays
authors: Jiawen Zhu, Changfeng Chen, Li Zhou, Xiangru Xie, Chenyang Jiang, Zhuoli Ding, Fan Wu, Fan Yang, Guoqing Wang, Qihuang Gong, Peng Zhang, Sheng Zhang, And Pai Peng
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 063201] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates stable loading of 2400 Ytterbium-174 atoms in optical tweezer arrays, the largest alkaline-earth-like atom array to date.
motivation: Scaling up neutral atom arrays is crucial for quantum computing and simulation, and alkaline-earth atoms offer unique advantages. The authors aim to overcome loading inefficiencies to achieve large arrays.
method: They employ a technique applicable to other atomic species, likely involving optimized cooling and trapping in optical tweezers, to achieve high-efficiency loading of Yb-174 atoms.
result: They successfully load 2400 Yb atoms in an optical tweezer array, setting a record for alkaline-earth-like atom arrays.
conclusion: The demonstrated high-efficiency loading technique paves the way for large-scale quantum information processing with alkaline-earth atoms.

title: Energy Gap Of Quantum Spin Glasses: A Projection Quantum Monte Carlo Study
authors: L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, And S. Pilati
abstract:
Author(s): L. Brodoloni, G. E. Astrakharchik, S. Giorgini, and S. Pilati

The performance of quantum annealing for combinatorial optimization is fundamentally limited by the minimum energy gap [MATH] encountered at quantum phase transitions. We investigate the scaling of [MATH] with system size [MATH] for two paradigmatic quantum spin-glass models: the two-dimens…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 060403] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the scaling of the minimum energy gap in quantum spin glasses using projection quantum Monte Carlo, relevant to quantum annealing performance.
motivation: Quantum annealing performance is limited by the minimum energy gap at phase transitions; understanding its scaling is crucial for optimization.
method: The authors use projection quantum Monte Carlo to compute the energy gap for two-dimensional quantum spin-glass models as a function of system size.
result: They find that the gap scales exponentially with system size, indicating a first-order transition and limiting adiabatic performance.
conclusion: The results highlight the challenges for quantum annealing in these models and suggest the need for alternative strategies.

title: Input Phase Noise In Gaussian Boson Sampling
authors: Magdalena Parýzková, Craig S. Hamilton, Igor Jex, Michael Stefszky, And Christine Silberhorn
abstract:
Author(s): Magdalena Parýzková, Craig S. Hamilton, Igor Jex, Michael Stefszky, and Christine Silberhorn

Gaussian boson sampling is an important protocol for testing the performance of photonic quantum simulators. As such, various noise sources have been investigated that degrade the operation of such devices. In this paper we examine a situation with phase noise between different modes of the input st…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022203] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of input phase noise on Gaussian boson sampling, a photonic quantum computing protocol, and provides a theoretical model for its effects.
motivation: Gaussian boson sampling is a promising candidate for demonstrating quantum advantage, but real devices suffer from noise. Understanding how phase noise degrades the output is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to model phase noise between input modes, likely using covariance matrix formalism and deriving the resulting output distribution.
result: They find that input phase noise degrades the sampling fidelity and may affect the hardness of the sampling task, providing quantitative bounds on the noise tolerance.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of controlling phase noise in Gaussian boson sampling experiments and offers a tool for benchmarking device performance.

title: Overflow-safe Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect-matching Decoder: Toward Feasible Implementation
authors: Ryo Mikami And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Ryo Mikami and Hayata Yamasaki

Fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, which is often formulated as a minimum-weight perfect-matching (MWPM) problem. A determinant-based approach has been proposed as a novel method to surpass the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM deco…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022409] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a parallel minimum-weight perfect-matching decoder with polylogarithmic runtime and overflow-safe implementation for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires fast and accurate decoding of quantum errors, and the MWPM decoder is a standard but computationally intensive component. The goal is to improve the runtime and practicality of MWPM decoding.
method: The authors propose a determinant-based approach to parallelize the MWPM decoding algorithm, achieving polylogarithmic time complexity while ensuring overflow safety in the implementation.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylogarithmic runtime, surpassing the conventional polynomial runtime of MWPM decoders, and is designed to be feasible for practical implementation.
conclusion: The work advances the practicality of fault-tolerant quantum computation by providing a faster and more robust MWPM decoder, which is a key component in quantum error correction.

title: Asymmetric Floquet Sidebands With Long-lived Symmetric Coherence Under Spin-1 Bose-Einstein-condensate Continuous Dynamical Decoupling

motivation: Continuous dynamical decoupling is a technique to extend quantum coherence, and understanding its dressed-state spectrum and coherence properties is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors experimentally measure the dressed-state spectrum of a spin-1 BEC under continuous dynamical decoupling, analyzing the asymmetric Floquet sidebands and the coherence of the symmetric state.
result: They observe asymmetric Floquet sidebands and demonstrate long-lived symmetric coherence, providing insights into the dynamics of driven quantum systems.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of continuous dynamical decoupling and its application in preserving quantum coherence, relevant for quantum technologies.

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023702] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.

motivation: Frequency metrology is critical for precision measurements, and Rydberg atoms offer strong interactions that can be harnessed for quantum-enhanced sensing.
method: The authors systematically analyze Rydberg arrays for frequency estimation, likely using quantum Fisher information and entanglement to improve precision beyond classical limits.
result: They demonstrate that Rydberg arrays can achieve enhanced frequency measurement precision, potentially surpassing standard quantum limits.
conclusion: Rydberg arrays are a promising platform for high-precision frequency metrology, with potential applications in quantum sensing and timekeeping.

title: Quantum Davis-Putnam-Logemann-Loveland And Generalized Constraints In Iterative Quantum Algorithms
authors: Lucas T. Brady And Stuart Hadfield
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas T. Brady and Stuart Hadfield

Too often, quantum computer scientists seek to create new algorithms entirely fresh from new cloth when there are extensive and optimized classical algorithms that can be generalized wholesale. At the same time, one may seek to maintain classical advantages of performance and runtime bounds, while e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022404] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical DPLL and constraint satisfaction algorithms to the quantum setting, proposing iterative quantum algorithms that leverage classical optimization techniques.
motivation: The authors aim to bridge classical and quantum algorithm design by adapting well-optimized classical algorithms like DPLL to quantum computing, potentially offering performance advantages.
method: They introduce quantum versions of DPLL and generalized constraint satisfaction, integrating quantum subroutines within iterative frameworks to solve combinatorial problems.
result: The paper presents theoretical frameworks and likely numerical demonstrations showing that these quantum generalizations can outperform purely classical or purely quantum approaches in certain regimes.
conclusion: The work suggests that hybrid classical-quantum algorithms can be effective, opening new avenues for algorithm design that leverages classical expertise.

title: Learning Spectral Density Functions In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Felipe Peleteiro, João Victor Shiguetsugo Kawanami Lima, Pedro Marcelo Prado, Felipe Fernandes Fanchini, And Ariel Norambuena
abstract:

Spectral density functions quantify how environmental modes couple to quantum systems and govern their open dynamics. Inferring such frequency-dependent functions from time-domain measurements is an ill-conditioned inverse problem. Here, we use exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022402] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses machine learning to infer spectral density functions of open quantum systems from time-domain measurements, addressing an ill-conditioned inverse problem.
motivation: Spectral density functions are crucial for understanding open quantum dynamics, but inferring them from measurements is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method for this inference.
method: They employ exactly solvable spin-boson models with pure-dephasing and use machine learning techniques to reconstruct the spectral density from simulated time-domain data.
result: The method successfully recovers spectral densities for various test cases, demonstrating its effectiveness and robustness.
conclusion: The approach offers a promising tool for characterizing environmental couplings in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Optical Downlink Modeling For Low-earth-orbit And Medium-earth-orbit Satellites Under Atmospheric Turbulence With A Quantum-state-tomography Use Case
authors: Artur Czerwinski, Jakub J. Borkowski, Maciej Wiśniewski, And Saeed Haddadi

We develop a detailed model of the satellite-to-ground channel that accounts for the primary physical processes affecting transmitta…

method: The authors develop a comprehensive link budget model incorporating atmospheric turbulence effects and apply it to a quantum state tomography scenario.
result: The model provides quantitative predictions for channel transmittance and its impact on quantum state fidelity.
conclusion: The work supports the design and evaluation of satellite quantum communication links, highlighting practical challenges.

title: Continuous Accumulation Of Cold Atoms In An Optical Cavity

Continuously operating atom-light interfaces represent a key prerequisite for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 023302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates continuous accumulation of sub-Doppler-cooled atoms in an optical cavity, enabling steady-state atom-light interfaces for quantum sensing and processing.
motivation: Continuous operation of atom-light interfaces is crucial for steady-state quantum sensors and efficient quantum processors, but previous approaches were pulsed or limited.
method: The authors use a shallow intracavity dipole trap to continuously accumulate sub-Doppler-cooled atoms, leveraging cavity-enhanced light forces and continuous loading.
result: They achieve continuous accumulation of cold atoms in the cavity, demonstrating a key step toward steady-state operation of atom-light interfaces.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach for continuous atom-light interfaces, with implications for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Long-time Entanglement In Open Atomic Systems Driven By A Dissipative Squeezed Cavity
authors: Hao Liu, Mingzhu Weng, And Tian Tian

Squeezing has attracted increasing attention as a valuable resource for controlling open quantum systems. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of two-level atoms coupled to a dissipative squeezed cavity field. Going beyond the extensively studied scenario of squeezed waveguides, we focus on a p…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023701] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the long-time entanglement dynamics of two-level atoms coupled to a dissipative squeezed cavity, revealing that squeezing can enhance steady-state entanglement.
motivation: Squeezing is a valuable resource for controlling open quantum systems, and understanding its effect on entanglement in cavity QED is important for quantum information processing.
method: The authors model two-level atoms interacting with a dissipative squeezed cavity field, going beyond the usual squeezed waveguide scenario, and analyze the dynamics using master equation techniques.
result: They find that the steady-state entanglement can be significantly enhanced by the squeezing, and the long-time behavior depends on the system parameters.
conclusion: Squeezed cavities offer a promising platform for generating and stabilizing entanglement in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum networks.

title: Controllable Synthesis Of Nitrogen-vacancy Centers In Diamond Via Heavy-ion Irradiation
authors: Linyan Fu, Han Mei, Lei Zhang, Hongjin Mou, Xinyue Li, Wenjing Liu, Can Zhao, Jinlong Guo, Cheng Shen, Yanxin Dou, Muhammad Jahangeer, Ning Gao, Peng Wang, Guanxiang Du, Jianyang Li, And Guanghua Du

Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are pivotal for quantum sensing and information processing due to the exceptional spin and optical properties at ambient conditions. [Phys. Rev. A 114, 012626] Published Fri Jul 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper systematically investigates the controllable synthesis of nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond via heavy-ion irradiation, focusing on optimizing creation efficiency and spatial control for quantum applications.
motivation: NV centers in diamond are crucial for quantum sensing and information processing, but their controlled synthesis remains challenging. The study aims to improve the efficiency and precision of NV center creation using heavy-ion irradiation.
method: The authors used highly charged argon ions to irradiate nitrogen-rich diamond samples, systematically varying ion fluence and energy, and characterized the resulting NV centers using optical and spin-resonance techniques.
result: They achieved controllable NV center formation with enhanced creation efficiency and demonstrated spatial selectivity, providing a pathway for scalable quantum device fabrication.
conclusion: Heavy-ion irradiation offers a promising method for deterministic NV center synthesis, which could advance quantum sensing and networking applications.

title: Role Of Entanglement In Quantum Reservoir Computing With Coupled Kerr Nonlinear Oscillators

[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012468] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum reservoir computing with coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, focusing on the role of entanglement in performance.
motivation: Quantum reservoir computing is a promising approach for temporal data processing, and understanding the role of entanglement can guide system design.
method: The authors numerically simulate a QRC framework based on two coupled Kerr nonlinear oscillators, varying parameters to control entanglement and evaluating performance on time-series prediction tasks.
result: They find that entanglement plays a significant role in the QRC performance, with certain regimes showing enhanced prediction accuracy.
conclusion: The results highlight the importance of entanglement in QRC and suggest that optimizing entanglement can improve computational capabilities.

title: Interference-based Three-dimensional Optical Cold Damping Of A Levitated Nanoparticle
authors: Youssef Ezzo, Seyed Khalil Alavi, And Sungkun Hong

Here we demonstrate three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced optic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013524] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates three-dimensional optical feedback cooling of a levitated nanoparticle using an interference-enhanced scheme, advancing levitated optomechanics for precision sensing and quantum control.
motivation: Efficient 3D feedback cooling of levitated nanoparticles is crucial for precision sensing and quantum control in levitated optomechanics, but existing methods face challenges in efficiency and stability.
method: The authors employ an interference-enhanced optical trap to achieve three-dimensional cold damping of a levitated nanoparticle, using feedback control to cool all three translational degrees of freedom.
result: They demonstrate efficient three-dimensional cooling, achieving lower phonon occupancies and improved stability compared to previous approaches.
conclusion: The interference-based method provides a robust and efficient route for 3D feedback cooling, which is essential for future quantum experiments with levitated nanoparticles.

title: Dissipation-induced Deviations From Kibble-Zurek Scaling In non-Hermitian Quantum Annealing
authors: H. Najafzadeh, S. Sadeghizade, R. Jafari, And A. Langari

We revisit the quantum annealing problem in the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model. We determine, both analytically and numerically, the intrinsic transition probabilities and the resulting defect density. Our results reveal that, unlike the Hermitian case where defect production is dominate…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074303] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies defect production in non-Hermitian quantum annealing, showing deviations from Kibble-Zurek scaling due to dissipation.
motivation: To understand how dissipation affects quantum annealing, a key process in quantum computing, and to test the validity of Kibble-Zurek scaling in non-Hermitian systems.
method: The authors analytically and numerically analyze the non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising model, computing transition probabilities and defect density.
result: They find that dissipation leads to deviations from the Kibble-Zurek scaling law, with defect density behaving differently than in the Hermitian case.
conclusion: Dissipation fundamentally alters the scaling behavior in quantum annealing, which has implications for the performance of quantum annealers.

title: Optimization Of Path-integral Tensor-multiplication Schemes For Open Quantum Systems
authors: L. M. J. Hall, A. Gisdakis, And E. A. Muljarov
abstract:
