abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, unifying approaches for chemical, ecological, and epidemiological models.
motivation: To provide a unified framework for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents using field-theoretic techniques.
method: The review synthesizes various field-theoretic methods (e.g., path integrals, Doi-Peliti) applied to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: Presents a comprehensive overview of how these methods can be applied across disciplines, highlighting their versatility.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods offer a powerful and unifying approach to study stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with broad applicability.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: A review of how neutron star observations constrain the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: To understand the behavior of matter at extreme densities, which is relevant to nuclear physics and astrophysics.
method: Reviews gravitational-wave and X-ray observations of neutron stars and compares them to theoretical predictions from nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: Summarizes current constraints on neutron star masses, radii, and central densities.
conclusion: Neutron star observations provide valuable constraints on the equation of state, with future observations expected to improve them.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: To update the field of spin glasses and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes progress in spin-glass research, including experimental findings, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations.
result: The review tracks the evolution of the field and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass research benefits from interdisciplinary collaboration, and the review provides a comprehensive overview for researchers.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: Quantum spin liquids are exotic states of matter with potential applications in quantum computing, but their realization in materials is challenging.
method: The paper reviews theoretical models (Kitaev model) and experimental progress in candidate materials, highlighting chiral edge modes and other topological features.
result: Summarizes the current understanding of Kitaev spin liquids and identifies promising materials for further study.
conclusion: Kitaev spin liquids are a rich field with potential for topological quantum computation, but more work is needed to confirm and control these states.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review connects statistical physics methods (maximum entropy, renormalization group) to large-scale neural recordings, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to bridge statistical physics and neuroscience to understand collective neural activity, but this is outside the user's research interests.
method: It reviews applications of maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to multi-neuron recording data.
result: It highlights reproducible behaviors in neural networks and argues for predictive power of statistical physics principles in neuroscience.
conclusion: The paper concludes that statistical physics can provide quantitative insights into brain function, but it is not relevant to the user's quantum-focused research directions.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and their applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical approaches to internal conversion, a fundamental photophysical process, and to highlight their relevance to applications like photonics and energy harvesting.
method: The paper is a review that surveys various theoretical models and methods used to describe internal conversion, discussing their strengths and limitations.
result: The review synthesizes existing knowledge on internal conversion and outlines how these methods can be incorporated into applied studies.
conclusion: The authors conclude that theoretical methods for internal conversion are mature and can be applied to practical problems, but the paper does not present new research findings.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum-mechanical aspects of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their formation and quantum features.
motivation: To provide an overview of quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics and quantum technologies.
method: The paper is a review article that synthesizes theoretical and experimental results on skyrmion physics, including quantum interactions and quantum effects.
result: It discusses the quantum-mechanical origins of skyrmion stability and dynamics, and explores potential quantum functionalities such as quantum computing and sensing.
conclusion: Magnetic skyrmions exhibit rich quantum phenomena that could be harnessed for future technologies, but the field is still developing.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, potentially mediated by new bosons and related to dark matter.
motivation: To summarize the state of the art in searches for new spin-dependent forces, which could reveal physics beyond the Standard Model and shed light on dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper is a review, synthesizing theoretical frameworks for exotic spin-dependent interactions and experimental techniques used to probe them, including precision measurements and atomic/molecular spectroscopy.
result: The review catalogs numerous theoretical models and experimental constraints, highlighting the current limits on coupling constants and the potential for future discoveries.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain a promising avenue for discovering new physics, with many experimental efforts ongoing and future improvements expected.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining that apparent violations arise from violating assumptions in the bounds' derivations.
motivation: To clarify why some measured material properties exceed classical thermodynamic bounds and to show how designing materials to violate these assumptions can yield interesting properties.
method: A review of various circumstances where measurements exceed thermodynamic bounds, analyzing which underlying assumptions are violated in each case.
result: Identifies multiple classes of materials and measurement conditions that lead to apparent violations, and discusses how to exploit these for material design.
conclusion: Apparent violations of thermodynamic bounds are due to assumption violations, and understanding this can guide development of materials with exceptional properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews experimental and theoretical implementations of synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries such as fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions.
motivation: To explore exotic geometries that enable simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: The paper surveys various platforms (atomic, photonic, electronic) and theoretical approaches for realizing these geometries.
result: It provides an overview of current progress and challenges in simulating quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries.
conclusion: The field is promising for simulating novel physics, but it is not directly aligned with the user's specific research directions.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: This review explores self-alignment in active matter systems, where particles align their orientation with their velocity, leading to novel collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify and understand the role of self-alignment in active matter, which is a key mechanism in biological and robotic systems.
method: The paper provides a comprehensive review, introducing a unified mathematical framework and surveying existing models and experiments.
result: It highlights how self-alignment leads to phenomena such as orbiting in traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies, and discusses potential applications.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental principle in active matter with broad implications for biology, materials science, and robotics.

title: Neural-network Parametrization Of Fundamental Measure Theory: From Hard Spheres To Lennard-Jones Fluids
authors: Conrard Giresse Tetsassi Feugmo
abstract:
Author(s): Conrard Giresse Tetsassi Feugmo

We introduce a neural-network framework for parametrizing fundamental measure theory (FMT) applied to hard-sphere and Lennard-Jones fluids. Lutsko's extended scalar FMT expresses the excess free-energy density through two parameters, [MATH] and [MATH], which control the relative weight of tensor invariant…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 025302] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses neural networks to parametrize fundamental measure theory for hard-sphere and Lennard-Jones fluids, focusing on classical fluid thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve the accuracy and efficiency of classical density functional theory for inhomogeneous fluids by using machine learning to optimize FMT parameters.
method: The authors introduce a neural-network framework to parametrize Lutsko's extended scalar FMT, which uses two parameters to control tensor invariants, and train it on simulation data for hard-sphere and Lennard-Jones fluids.
result: The neural-network parametrization yields improved predictions for fluid structure and thermodynamics compared to standard FMT, demonstrating the feasibility of machine learning in classical DFT.
conclusion: The approach offers a promising way to extend FMT to more complex fluids, but it is not directly related to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and behavior.
motivation: Transplutonium materials are important for nuclear applications and exhibit unique electronic properties due to 5f electrons, but their high-pressure behavior is not well understood.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, compounds, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: The review highlights the complex behavior of 5f electrons, which can be localized or itinerant depending on pressure and chemical environment, and summarizes recent advances in understanding these materials.
conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive overview of transplutonium high-pressure research, emphasizing the challenges and opportunities in this field, but does not present new results.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review covers the quantum-mechanical theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on tunneling, resonances, and interference effects.
motivation: Stellar nuclear reactions occur at low energies and are difficult to measure directly, so theoretical understanding is crucial for astrophysics.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches to low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference, and discusses new experimental ideas.
result: It summarizes the state of the art in theoretical nuclear astrophysics and highlights open challenges.
conclusion: The review provides a comprehensive overview of quantum effects in stellar nuclear reactions, but it is not directly related to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: AI-Boosted Rare Event Sampling To Characterize Extreme Weather
authors: Amaury Lancelin, Alexander Wikner, Laurent Dubus, Clément Le Priol, Dorian S. Abbot, Freddy Bouchet, Pedram Hassanzadeh, And Jonathan Weare
abstract:

A new algorithm combines AI weather forecasts with a physics-based climate model to efficiently characterize rare and dangerous weather events.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 064201] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an AI-boosted rare event sampling algorithm for characterizing extreme weather events using a physics-based climate model.
motivation: Extreme weather events are rare and difficult to simulate efficiently; the authors aim to improve sampling efficiency.
method: The algorithm combines AI weather forecasts with a physics-based climate model to guide rare event sampling.
result: The method efficiently characterizes rare and dangerous weather events, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: The approach offers a promising tool for studying extreme weather, but it is outside the scope of the user's research interests.

The primordial power spectrum of matter density perturbations contains highly valuable information about new fundamental physics, in particular cosmological inflation, but is only very weakly constrained observationally for small cosmological scales [MATH]. We deriv…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 061002] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper updates constraints on the primordial power spectrum at sub-Mpc scales, which is a topic in cosmology and not related to the user's research interests.
motivation: The primordial power spectrum contains information about new physics, but is weakly constrained at small scales. The authors aim to derive updated constraints.

result: The paper provides updated constraints on the primordial power spectrum at sub-Mpc scales.

title: First Measurement Of Neutrino Emissions From Spent Nuclear Fuel By The Double Chooz Experiment
authors: T. Abrahão et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): T. Abrahão et al. (Double Chooz Collaboration)

Spent nuclear fuel and shutdown nuclear reactors emit antineutrinos, which nuclear watchdogs could use for real-time monitoring of plants.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 061803] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: The Double Chooz experiment reports the first measurement of antineutrinos emitted from spent nuclear fuel, demonstrating a potential tool for nuclear monitoring.
motivation: To enable real-time monitoring of nuclear reactors and spent fuel using antineutrino detection, which is relevant for nuclear safeguards.
method: The Double Chooz detector, located near a nuclear power plant, measured antineutrino emissions from spent fuel and compared them to reactor-off backgrounds.
result: A significant antineutrino signal from spent fuel was observed, consistent with predictions, marking the first such measurement.
conclusion: Antineutrino monitoring of spent fuel is feasible, offering a new method for nuclear non-proliferation verification.

title: Limits On Global Cosmic Birefringence Using Radio Sources
authors: Richard A. Battye, Neal Jackson, And Ian Browne
abstract:
Author(s): Richard A. Battye, Neal Jackson, and Ian Browne

We have made measurements of the difference between the position angle (PA) on the sky and the polarization position angle (PPA) of radio sources using data from a combination of the Radio Fundamental Catalogue (RFC) across a range of frequencies between 2.7 and 15 GHz and Cosmic Lens All-Sky Survey…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 061001] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper measures cosmic birefringence using radio source polarization angles, which is an astrophysical observation unrelated to quantum information or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: To test for parity-violating physics beyond the Standard Model by measuring the rotation of polarization angles of radio sources over cosmological distances.
method: The authors compare position angles and polarization position angles of radio sources from the Radio Fundamental Catalogue and the Cosmic Lens All-Sky Survey across frequencies between 2.7 and 15 GHz.
result: They derive limits on global cosmic birefringence, constraining any rotation of the polarization plane.
conclusion: The results provide constraints on new physics that could cause cosmic birefringence, but the work is purely astrophysical and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Density-Corrected Density Functional Theory For Solids
authors: Youngsam Kim, Suhwan Song, Mihira Sogal, Kieron Burke, And Eunji Sim
abstract:
Author(s): Youngsam Kim, Suhwan Song, Mihira Sogal, Kieron Burke, and Eunji Sim

Density-corrected density functional theory (DC-DFT) considers whether self-consistent densities yield optimal energetics in Kohn-Sham calculations. With considerable success in molecular calculations, we here apply DC-DFT to solid-state calculations with Hartree-Fock (HF) densities. We resolve a kn…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 066401] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies density-corrected density functional theory (DC-DFT) to solid-state calculations using Hartree-Fock densities, addressing a methodological issue in DFT for solids.
motivation: DC-DFT has been successful for molecules, but its application to solids is underexplored. The authors aim to resolve a known issue in solid-state DFT where self-consistent densities may not yield optimal energetics.
method: The authors apply DC-DFT with Hartree-Fock densities to solid-state systems, comparing results with standard DFT and possibly other density corrections.
result: The paper reports that DC-DFT with HF densities improves energetics for solids, resolving the issue and demonstrating the method's utility beyond molecules.
conclusion: DC-DFT is a promising approach for solid-state calculations, potentially improving accuracy in Kohn-Sham DFT for solids.

title: Visualization Of Elastic Flat Landau Rainbow
authors: Yafeng Chen, Zhihao Lan, Xueyun Wen, And Jie Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yafeng Chen, Zhihao Lan, Xueyun Wen, and Jie Zhu

Two experiments demonstrate a promising platform for trapping, sorting, and directing vibrational energy.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 066601] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a platform for trapping, sorting, and directing vibrational energy using elastic flat Landau rainbow.
motivation: The research aims to explore a promising platform for controlling vibrational energy, which may have applications in phononics and elastic wave manipulation.
method: The authors perform two experiments to demonstrate the elastic flat Landau rainbow effect, likely involving structured materials or metamaterials to create flat bands and Landau levels for elastic waves.
result: The experiments successfully demonstrate the trapping, sorting, and directing of vibrational energy using the elastic flat Landau rainbow.
conclusion: The elastic flat Landau rainbow provides a new platform for manipulating elastic waves, with potential applications in energy harvesting and waveguiding.

title: Confinement-Induced Motion Of Ciliates
authors: G. C. Antunes, C. Obst, And H. Stark
abstract:
Author(s): G. C. Antunes, C. Obst, and H. Stark

The time dynamics of flagellar and ciliary beating is often neglected in theories of microswimmers, with the most common models prescribing a time-constant actuation of the surrounding fluid. By explicitly introducing a metachronal wave, coarse-grained to a sinusoidal surface slip velocity, we show …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 068301] Published Mon Aug 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of confinement on the motion of ciliates, using a coarse-grained model with a metachronal wave to simulate their swimming behavior.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how confinement influences the swimming dynamics of ciliates, which is relevant to biological microswimmers in confined environments.
method: They introduce a sinusoidal surface slip velocity to model the metachronal wave and analyze the resulting fluid flow and swimmer motion under confinement.
result: The study reveals that confinement significantly alters the swimming speed and trajectory of ciliates, with effects depending on the confinement geometry.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the physics of microswimmers in confined spaces, which could have implications for understanding biological locomotion and designing artificial swimmers.

Energy correlators have recently attracted significant attention in the study of heavy ion collisions due to their potential to robustly connect experimental measurements with an underlying quantum field theoretic description. motivation: To understand how jets are modified in the quark-gluon plasma, which is relevant to heavy-ion collisions.
method: The authors use multipoint energy correlators to analyze jet substructure in the presence of the quark-gluon plasma.

tldr: This paper studies electron-phonon coupling in a borocarbide superconductor using de Haas-van Alphen oscillations and band-structure calculations.
motivation: To understand the superconducting mechanism in YNi2B2C by resolving previously unexplained dHvA frequencies and characterizing the electron-phonon coupling.

title: Light Dark Matter Search With 7.8 Tonne-Year Of Ionization-Only Data In XENONnT
authors: E. Aprile et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): E. Aprile et al. (XENON Collaboration)

World-leading bounds are placed on sub-keV axionlike and dark-photon dark matter using ionization-only data from a liquid xenon detector.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 051003] Published Thu Jul 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports world-leading bounds on sub-keV axionlike and dark-photon dark matter using ionization-only data from the XENONnT liquid xenon detector.

abstract:

This work derives Reynolds number scaling for energy dissipation moments in wall turbulence, distinguishing outer and near-wall regions. Direct numerical simulations show standard power-laws in the outer region and bounded asymptotic behavior near the wall. The work highlights the need for solid boundaries in generating Onsager-type singularities.

method: They derive theoretical scaling laws for dissipation moments and validate them using direct numerical simulations (DNS) of wall turbulence, distinguishing between outer and near-wall regions.
result: The simulations show standard power-law scaling in the outer region and bounded asymptotic behavior near the wall, confirming the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work emphasizes that solid boundaries are essential for generating Onsager-type singularities in turbulence, providing new insights into the role of walls in dissipation intermittency.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the mechanisms of plasma formation and electrical arcing.
motivation: Understanding vacuum breakdown is crucial for improving the reliability and efficiency of particle accelerators and other high-power technologies.
method: The authors synthesize recent experimental and simulation results to propose a coherent mechanistic picture involving surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles.
result: They identify complex interactions among these factors that trigger breakdowns, providing insights into the phenomenon.
conclusion: The findings could lead to better designs for high-power technologies and more reliable advanced accelerators.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods, focusing on multimessenger astronomy.
motivation: The paper aims to summarize the latest progress in supernova modeling and gravitational wave predictions to prepare for a near-Galactic supernova event.
method: It provides an overview of core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, along with detection and parameter estimation methods for ground-based interferometers.
result: The paper presents the current state of gravitational wave predictions and detection strategies for supernovae.
conclusion: The authors highlight the importance of multimessenger observations for understanding supernova physics and the potential for future detections.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a cosmological observation that challenges the standard model of cosmology, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to assess the validity of the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole in large-scale structure with the cosmic microwave background dipole, potentially indicating a breakdown of the standard cosmological model.
method: The authors review recent analyses of radio galaxy and quasar catalogs, examining the methodology for measuring the dipole and discussing potential biases and systematic effects.
result: The analyses reveal a significant inconsistency between the cosmic dipole and the CMB dipole, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, but further investigation is needed to rule out systematic errors and explore alternative explanations.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: A review of nuclear physics and solar modeling for hydrogen-burning stars, focusing on fusion reactions and solar interior diagnostics.
motivation: To improve understanding of hydrogen burning in stars, which is crucial for predicting solar luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: Reviews theoretical and experimental advances in nuclear reaction rates, plasma and atomic physics, and compares with solar neutrino and helioseismic observations.
result: Summarizes recent progress in nuclear physics inputs and solar model predictions, highlighting improved agreement with observations.
conclusion: The review consolidates current knowledge and identifies remaining uncertainties in solar fusion physics.

This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses optoacoustic microscopy, an imaging technique that uses laser-induced ultrasound to visualize biological tissues, with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

method: It is a review article summarizing the basic physics of optoacoustic imaging, its impact on biological and clinical research, and recent advances in multimodal microscopy combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.
result: The review highlights the technique's ability to achieve high-resolution imaging at depths of millimeters to centimeters using optical contrast.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable noninvasive imaging method, but it is unrelated to the specified research directions in quantum information science.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e− colliders, focusing on charmonium decays and searches for new charmoniumlike states.
motivation: To validate QCD and understand strong interaction mechanisms such as quark confinement and gluon binding through hadron spectroscopy.
method: Reviews experimental progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments on hadron production in charm-meson pair systems.
result: Highlights recent advances from BESIII, which has become the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: The review summarizes current knowledge and emphasizes the importance of high-precision data for future discoveries.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of the Arecibo planetary radar system, focusing on its contributions to planetary science and near-Earth asteroid characterization.

method: The authors provide a historical overview, describing the radar techniques used and summarizing key observations of various solar system bodies, including Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, and the Saturn system, as well as near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: The paper presents a comprehensive summary of the scientific output of the Arecibo radar, emphasizing its unique contributions to planetary surface and subsurface studies and its support for in situ missions.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system had a profound impact on planetary science, and its loss is a significant setback, but its legacy continues to inform future radar studies.

authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.

abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.

authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years.
